Noise reduction while riding is as much about helping to manage and reduce fatigue as it is hearing protection. Wind noise is one of our biggest opponents for hearing safety on the bike. It doesn't take long to do permanent damage at road speeds. The charts below show decibel loudness of common things and how long until damage occurs.

 

Sustained noise also leads to fatigue. Sam Marcora from the Univerity of Kent writes a good bit about this: http://adventure-motorcycling.blogspot.com/p/fatigue.html

Interesting. Thanks for the post. I didn't realize the noise from wind was that loud. It got me curious and I found this:

  • There is no significant difference in wind noise level as a function of speed, no matter what the helmet brand or model (all being full coverage).
  • Neither the riding position nor the brand or style of motorcycle make significant difference in noise level.
  • Padding inside the helmet, open or closed vents, or added weather stripping on the helmet to alter flow patterns, does not significantly alter the noise level in a helmet.
  • Stopped at a stop light at a busy intersection with your helmet visor closed produces a sound level of 80-90dB SPL. (Lawn mower, loud restaurant levels)
  • When not wearing a helmet, the wind noise at highway speed is nearly 10 times greater than when wearing a full coverage helmet.
  • Below 30mph, machine, exhaust and environmental noises are heard. Once speeds exceed approximately 30mph, wind noise dominates completely.
  • Some helmets resonate at approximately 500Hz, and actually enhance wind noise.
  • Legal speeds of 65mph can produce wind noise levels at 103dB SPL, (chainsaw, pneumatic drill). This noise is loud enough to cause TTS in your hearing, tinnitus and permanent ear damage.

I disagree with some of your findings. I've only been riding on road bikes for a couple of years but used to ride dirt bikes when I was younger. I cant recall accurately but Im pretty sure racing around the paddocks without a helmet on a dirt bike had none of the wind noise compared with what I experience riding my road bike these days.

What I do know is that a correct fitting helmet is a blessing especially when it comes to wind noise. When I purchased my road bike I was in a bit of a rush to purchase the gear, in a city that didnt have a lot of variety. Concerned about safety, I purchased a $800rrp (AUD) shoei helmet which wasnt too bad at first but within a couple of weeks I notices the noise starting. I did upgrade the pads to thicker ones and also found ear pads. Still not great.

So with my frustration building I aquired my old mans (10-15yr) old road HJC helmet and immeadiately noticed a massive difference. I actually used it for about a year while doing alot of reading about shapes and noise (a lot here and on other pages on the site : [http://www.webbikeworld.com/motorcycle-helmets/motorcycle-helmet-shapes.htm] ). Since then I have purchased and Aria and am pretty happy with it. I also have a mate who puts race tape over all the vent lips on his helmet and said that it helps alot. I am yet to try it but its something to think off. I also did put a double bubble screen on which improved this a bit as well. Getting in a full tuck behind this makes 200km/h speed

As for loud pipes, my bikes is reasonable but I cant hear it once im more then 70km/h or so (as per above).

For now I will wear ear plugs everywhere except for a 5 minute trip where the speed is below 60km/h. I do have hearing damage so I am very cautious with this these days.
